chunks.chunk_text: This policy defines the types of leave available to employees, eligibility conditions, accrual mechanics, and the approval process. It applies to all full-time employees on the company payroll, including those on hybrid or remote arrangements under the Remote Work Policy. Interns and contractors are governed by separate terms specified in their engagement letters and are not covered by this policy unless explicitly stated.

2.1 Full-time employees accrue 1.75 days of annual leave per completed month of service, up to a maximum of 21 days per calendar year. Accrual begins from the first full month of employment; the joining month is prorated based on the number of remaining working days.
2.2 Annual leave must be requested through the HR portal at least 5 working days in advance. Requests submitted with less notice may still be approved at the manager's discretion but are not guaranteed, particularly during peak project periods.
2.3 Unused annual leave may be carried forward, but a maximum of 5 days may be carried into the next calendar year. Any balance beyond 5 days is forfeited as of December 31st unless the employee's manager grants a written exception (see Section 2.4). Forfeited leave is not converted to a cash payout.
2.4 Exception: Employees on active client-critical projects, as designated by their reporting manager in writing, may carry forward up to 10 days with HR approval. This exception must be requested before December 1st and re-confirmed annually; it does not automatically renew from one year to the next.
2.5 Leave taken during a public holiday that falls within an approved leave period is not deducted from the employee's leave balance; the system automatically excludes gazetted holidays from the count.

3.1 Employees are entitled to 12 days of paid sick leave per calendar year, credited in full at the start of the year rather than accrued monthly.
3.2 Sick leave exceeding 2 consecutive days requires a medical certificate submitted within 3 working days of return. A single-day sick leave does not require documentation but repeated single-day absences (more than 4 in a rolling 3-month period) may trigger a manager check-in.
3.3 Sick leave does not carry forward to the next calendar year and has no cash-equivalent payout on exit.
3.4 Sick leave taken while on approved annual leave converts the affected days back to sick leave, provided a medical certificate is furnished; the annual leave balance is restored accordingly.

4.1 Primary caregivers are entitled to 90 calendar days of paid parental leave, inclusive of weekends and public holidays falling within the period.
4.2 Secondary caregivers are entitled to 14 calendar days of paid parental leave, which may be split into two blocks within 6 months of the birth or adoption date, subject to manager agreement on timing.
4.3 Parental leave must be requested at least 30 days before the expected start date, except in cases of premature birth or medical emergency, where retroactive approval within 7 days of the leave starting is permitted.
4.4 Adoptive parents are entitled to the same parental leave terms as biological parents, effective from the date of legal custody transfer.

5.1 Unpaid leave of up to 30 days may be requested for personal reasons, subject to manager and HR approval. Approval is not guaranteed and depends on business need and prior leave usage patterns.
5.2 Unpaid leave exceeding 30 days requires Director-level approval and may affect benefit continuity, including health insurance coverage, which is suspended after 45 consecutive days of unpaid leave unless the employee opts to self-fund premiums during that period.

6.1 Employees may take up to 3 days of emergency leave per year for family emergencies, bereavement, or unforeseen circumstances, without advance notice, subject to notifying the manager within 24 hours by any reasonable means (call, message, or email).
6.2 Emergency leave beyond 3 days in a year is deducted from the annual leave balance, or treated as unpaid leave if the annual balance is exhausted.

7.1 Annual leave may not be availed during the final 15 days of a resignation notice period unless mutually agreed upon with the manager in writing, to allow for adequate handover.
7.2 Any unused annual leave balance at the time of exit, up to the standard cap in Section 2.1, is paid out as part of the final settlement, calculated on the employee's last drawn basic salary.

This policy governs business travel booking, reimbursable expenses, and approval thresholds for all employees traveling on company business, whether domestic or international. It does not cover relocation expenses, which are governed under a separate Relocation Policy.

2.1 All domestic and international travel must be booked through the approved corporate travel portal, which provides negotiated rates and ensures travel insurance is automatically applied.
2.2 Economy class is the default for flights under 6 hours. Business class is permitted for flights exceeding 6 hours, subject to manager approval, and should be booked at least 10 days in advance where possible to control cost.
2.3 Exception: Employees with a documented medical condition may be approved for business class regardless of flight duration, with HR and medical documentation on file. This exception is reviewed annually and does not require re-approval for each trip once on file.
2.4 Same-day return trips under 3 hours' flight time do not require advance manager sign-off but must still be logged in the travel portal for insurance and duty-of-care purposes.

3.1 Hotel bookings must not exceed the city-tier cap published annually by Finance (Tier 1 cities: USD 220/night; Tier 2: USD 150/night; Tier 3: USD 100/night). The current city-tier list is maintained on the Finance intranet page and updated each January.
3.2 Bookings exceeding the cap require pre-approval from the department head, with a brief justification (e.g., conference venue pricing, safety considerations in the destination city).
3.3 Extended stays for project reasons (beyond 14 consecutive nights) may qualify for a long-stay corporate rate; employees should contact the Travel Desk directly rather than booking through the standard portal.

4.1 A daily per-diem of USD 60 is provided for international travel and USD 35 for domestic travel, covering meals and incidentals. Per-diem is paid regardless of actual spend and does not require receipts.
4.2 Per-diem is not provided for days where meals are included in a conference or client event; the per-diem for that day is reduced by 50% if only one meal is covered, and to zero if two or more meals are covered.
4.3 The day of departure and the day of return are each paid at 75% of the standard per-diem rate to reflect partial-day travel.

5.1 Ride-hailing and taxi expenses are reimbursable with itemized receipts, including airport transfers and client-site travel.
5.2 Rental cars require pre-approval and are limited to mid-size vehicles unless client-facing requirements dictate otherwise (e.g., transporting equipment or multiple colleagues).
5.3 Personal vehicle use for business travel is reimbursed at the company's published per-kilometer rate, reviewed annually, and does not include fuel receipts separately.

6.1 Expense reports must be submitted within 14 calendar days of trip completion, through the expense management system with scanned receipts attached.
6.2 Reports submitted after 30 days will not be reimbursed except with Finance Director exception approval, which must include a written reason for the delay.
6.3 All expenses over USD 25 require an itemized receipt; expenses under USD 25 may use a self-declared entry, capped at USD 100 in self-declared entries per trip.
6.4 Expenses submitted in a foreign currency are converted using the exchange rate on the date of transaction, as sourced automatically by the expense system.

7.1 The following are not reimbursable under any circumstance: personal entertainment, alcohol not part of a client meal, traffic or parking fines, spa or minibar charges, and travel insurance already covered by the corporate policy.
7.2 Alcohol as part of a client meal is reimbursable up to a reasonable limit (generally interpreted as no more than 2 drinks per attendee) and must be itemized separately from food on the receipt where possible.

8.1 Employees traveling internationally for business must confirm visa and vaccination requirements with the Travel Desk at least 21 days prior to departure.
8.2 Visa application fees and related administrative costs for business travel are reimbursable; visas required for personal travel extensions attached to a business trip are not.

This policy sets expectations for employees working outside a company office, covering hybrid arrangements, fully remote work, and cross-border remote work. It applies to all full-time employees; interns and fixed-term contractors require explicit written approval from HR to work remotely under any arrangement.

2.1 Employees who have completed 3 months of continuous service are eligible to apply for a hybrid work arrangement, submitted through the HR portal with manager co-sign-off.
2.2 New hires within their first 3 months must work from the office unless the role is designated fully remote at time of hiring, in which case the offer letter will state this explicitly.
2.3 Eligibility may be paused for employees on a Performance Improvement Plan, at the manager's discretion, until performance concerns are resolved.

3.1 Standard hybrid arrangement permits up to 2 remote days per week, to be agreed upon with the immediate manager and documented in the team's working pattern log.
3.2 Teams with client-facing or on-site infrastructure responsibilities may have reduced remote-day allowances, as defined by the department head; any such restriction must be communicated to affected employees in writing.
3.3 Remote days may be swapped within the same week with manager approval (e.g., swapping a Tuesday for a Thursday) but do not carry over into the following week.

4.1 Fully remote arrangements (beyond 2 days/week) require Director-level approval and a documented business justification, reviewed every 6 months.
4.2 Fully remote employees must be reachable during core hours (10:00–16:00 local office time) unless otherwise agreed, and are expected to attend at least one in-person team gathering per quarter where feasible.
4.3 Fully remote status does not change an employee's designated work location for payroll, tax, or benefits purposes unless a separate relocation process has been completed.

5.1 Working remotely from a country other than the employee's registered work location requires prior approval from HR and Legal due to tax and compliance implications, and must be requested at least 15 working days in advance.
5.2 Such arrangements are capped at 20 working days per calendar year unless a separate international remote work agreement is signed. This cap resets each calendar year and does not accrue or carry forward.
5.3 Exception: This cap does not apply to employees on an approved international assignment, who are instead governed by the terms of their assignment letter.
5.4 Employees must not work from a country under active company travel restriction or sanctions watch, as published by the Legal team, regardless of remote work eligibility otherwise.

6.1 The company provides a laptop and standard peripherals for remote work; home internet and furniture are the employee's responsibility unless a stipend is separately approved for the role or location.
6.2 Remote employees must connect to company systems only via the corporate VPN and must not use public, unsecured Wi-Fi for work involving confidential data, per the Information Security Policy.
6.3 Loss or damage of company equipment while working remotely must be reported to IT within 24 hours, consistent with incident reporting timelines in the Information Security Policy.

7.1 Remote work privileges may be revoked by a manager if attendance in required meetings or delivery timelines are not consistently met, following at least one documented coaching conversation.
7.2 Repeated unavailability during core hours without prior notice may result in the employee being reverted to a full in-office schedule for a probationary review period of 60 days.

This policy defines minimum security requirements for protecting company and client data across all employees, contractors, and systems. It applies regardless of whether an employee is working from an office, home, or while traveling, and takes precedence over convenience when the two conflict.

2.1 All company accounts must use multi-factor authentication (MFA) where technically available, using either an authenticator app or hardware token; SMS-based MFA is permitted only as a fallback where no other option exists.
2.2 Passwords must be at least 12 characters, changed every 180 days, and must not be reused across the last 5 passwords. Passwords must combine upper case, lower case, numbers, and at least one symbol.
2.3 Shared or generic accounts (e.g., team mailboxes) are discouraged; where unavoidable, they must have a designated owner and a password rotation logged with IT every 90 days.

3.1 Data is classified into four tiers: Public, Internal, Confidential, and Restricted. Classification should be applied at the point of creation and re-evaluated if the data's sensitivity changes.
3.2 Restricted data (e.g., client PII, financial records, health information) must never be stored on personal devices or personal cloud storage, and must not be emailed to personal addresses under any circumstance.
3.3 Confidential data may be stored on company-managed devices only, with encryption at rest enabled; it may be shared externally only through approved secure-transfer tools, not standard email attachments.
3.4 Internal data may be shared within the company freely but should not be posted to public or external-facing platforms without a classification review.

4.1 All company laptops must have disk encryption, endpoint detection software, and automatic screen lock after 5 minutes of inactivity. These controls are enforced centrally by IT and cannot be disabled by the end user.
4.2 Personal devices used for email access (BYOD) must be enrolled in the mobile device management (MDM) system, which allows the company to remotely wipe corporate data (not personal data) if the device is lost or the employee exits.
4.3 USB storage devices are disabled by default on company laptops; exceptions require a documented business reason and IT approval, logged with an expiry date.

5.1 Any suspected security incident (phishing, data leak, lost device, unauthorized access) must be reported to the Security team within 1 hour of discovery, via the dedicated incident hotline or security@company email.
5.2 Failure to report a known incident within 24 hours is treated as a policy violation subject to disciplinary review, regardless of whether the incident ultimately caused harm.
5.3 The Security team will acknowledge receipt of a report within 2 hours during business hours and provide an initial assessment within 1 business day.

6.1 Confidential or Restricted data must not be entered into unapproved third-party AI tools or public generative AI services, including for tasks like summarization or translation.
6.2 Only AI tools listed on the Approved Tools Registry may be used for work involving company data; the registry is maintained by the Security team and reviewed quarterly.
6.3 New third-party tool requests (AI or otherwise) that would process company data must go through a vendor security review before adoption, even for free or trial tiers.

7.1 Security exceptions (e.g., use of an unapproved tool for a time-boxed pilot) require sign-off from the CISO and must be logged in the Exception Register with an expiry date, after which the exception automatically lapses unless renewed.
7.2 Exceptions involving Restricted data require an additional Legal review before approval, given regulatory and contractual implications.

This guide outlines the steps and timelines for new employee onboarding, from offer acceptance through the end of the probation period. It is intended for use by new hires, their managers, and HR business partners coordinating the process.

2.1 New hires receive a welcome email with joining instructions no later than 5 working days before their start date, including IT setup steps and a first-day agenda.
2.2 Background verification must be completed before the start date; if incomplete, joining may be deferred by up to 15 days. HR will communicate any deferral to the new hire at least 3 working days before the original start date.
2.3 New hires are asked to complete a pre-joining information form (emergency contact, bank details, ID documents) at least 3 working days before their start date to avoid Day One delays.

3.1 New hires must complete ID badge issuance, laptop handover, and IT account activation on their first day, coordinated by the assigned HR representative.
3.2 A buddy is assigned to every new hire for the first 30 days to assist with onboarding questions, informal team introductions, and navigating internal systems.
3.3 Managers are expected to hold a first-day 1:1 with the new hire covering role expectations, immediate priorities, and an introduction to the team's working norms.

4.1 New hires must complete Information Security Awareness training within the first 7 working days, covering password hygiene, phishing recognition, and data classification basics from the Information Security Policy.
4.2 New hires must complete Code of Conduct and Anti-Harassment training within the first 30 days, delivered through the Learning Management System.
4.3 Failure to complete mandatory training within the specified window results in automatic escalation to the employee's manager and HR, and repeated non-completion may result in restricted system access until training is finished.
4.4 Role-specific compliance training (e.g., for Finance, Legal, or client-facing roles) is assigned separately by the relevant department and is not covered by this general guide.

5.1 The standard probation period is 90 days from the date of joining, during which performance and cultural fit are assessed against role expectations shared at Day One.
5.2 Probation may be extended by up to 30 days at the manager's discretion if performance expectations are not yet met, with written notice to the employee explaining the reason and revised expectations.
5.3 A formal probation review meeting must be held between the manager and employee before the 90-day mark, with the outcome (confirmation, extension, or non-confirmation) documented in the HR system.

6.1 New hires must submit signed copies of the Employment Agreement, NDA, and Code of Conduct acknowledgment within the first week, uploaded through the HR portal.
6.2 Bank details for payroll must be submitted before the first payroll cycle to avoid delayed payment; late submission may push the first payment to the following cycle.
6.3 Employees changing bank details after joining must update them through the HR portal at least 5 working days before the next payroll run.

7.1 Standard equipment (laptop, headset, access card) is issued on Day One. Additional equipment requests must go through the IT Request Portal and are subject to role-based approval.
7.2 Equipment for remote or hybrid new hires is shipped in advance of the start date where the new hire's designated work location is more than 50km from the nearest office, coordinated with the IT logistics team.
This policy defines acceptable use of company IT systems, email, and internet access by all employees, contractors, and interns using company-owned or company-managed devices and accounts.

2.1 Company systems are provided primarily for business purposes. Limited, reasonable personal use is permitted provided it does not interfere with work duties, consume excessive bandwidth, or violate other company policies.
2.2 Employees must not use company systems to access, store, or distribute illegal, offensive, or discriminatory content, including content that violates the company's Anti-Harassment policy.
2.3 Personal use of company systems for outside business activities (e.g., running a personal side business) is not permitted at any time.

3.1 Company email must not be used to send Confidential or Restricted data to personal or unauthorized external email addresses, consistent with the data handling rules in the Information Security Policy.
3.2 Mass emails to all-staff distribution lists require approval from the Communications team, submitted at least 2 working days in advance except for urgent operational announcements.
3.3 Auto-forwarding of company email to personal or external accounts is disabled by default and may only be enabled with a documented business justification approved by IT Security.

4.1 Employees must not install unlicensed or unapproved software on company devices, including free or open-source tools not already on the approved software list.
4.2 Software installation requests must go through IT and be limited to tools relevant to the employee's role; requests are typically reviewed within 3 working days.
4.3 Browser extensions that request access to browsing data or credentials require IT approval before installation on company devices.

5.1 Access to peer-to-peer file sharing, torrenting, and unauthorized proxy/VPN services on company networks is prohibited at all times.
5.2 Reasonable personal browsing during breaks is permitted; excessive personal use affecting productivity may be addressed by the manager as a performance matter rather than a policy violation in most cases.
5.3 Streaming of high-bandwidth personal content (video, music) during work hours should be limited, particularly when connected via VPN, to avoid degrading network performance for business-critical applications.

6.1 Employees must not represent official company positions on personal social media accounts without authorization from the Communications team.
6.2 Sharing Confidential or Restricted company information on any public platform is strictly prohibited, including screenshots of internal tools, dashboards, or client materials.
6.3 Employees are encouraged to add a standard disclaimer ("views are my own") when discussing industry topics related to their role on personal social media.

7.1 The company reserves the right to monitor use of company-owned systems and networks for security and compliance purposes, in accordance with applicable local law.
7.2 Monitoring data is retained for a maximum of 12 months except where required for an active investigation, and access to monitoring data is restricted to authorized Security and HR personnel.

8.1 Violations of this policy may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination, depending on severity, as determined by HR and Legal.
8.2 First-time minor violations (e.g., installing a low-risk unapproved tool) typically result in a documented warning and required remediation rather than immediate escalation, unless combined with a data security breach.

2.1 Full-time employees accrue 1.75 days of annual leave per completed month of service, up to a maximum of 21 days per calendar year. Accrual begins from the first full month of employment; the joining month is prorated based on the number of remaining working days.
2.2 Annual leave must be requested through the HR portal at least 5 working days in advance. Requests submitted with less notice may still be approved at the manager's discretion but are not guaranteed, particularly during peak project periods.
2.3 Unused annual leave may be carried forward, but a maximum of 5 days may be carried into the next calendar year. Any balance beyond 5 days is forfeited as of December 31st unless the employee's manager grants a written exception (see Section 2.4). Forfeited leave is not converted to a cash payout.
2.4 Exception: Employees on active client-critical projects, as designated by their reporting manager in writing, may carry forward up to 10 days with HR approval. This exception must be requested before December 1st and re-confirmed annually; it does not automatically renew from one year to the next.
2.5 Leave taken during a public holiday that falls within an approved leave period is not deducted from the employee's leave balance; the system automatically excludes gazetted holidays from the count.

7.1 Annual leave may not be availed during the final 15 days of a resignation notice period unless mutually agreed upon with the manager in writing, to allow for adequate handover.
7.2 Any unused annual leave balance at the time of exit, up to the standard cap in Section 2.1, is paid out as part of the final settlement, calculated on the employee's last drawn basic salary.

This policy defines the types of leave available to employees, eligibility conditions, accrual mechanics, and the approval process. It applies to all full-time employees on the company payroll, including those on hybrid or remote arrangements under the Remote Work Policy. Interns and contractors are governed by separate terms specified in their engagement letters and are not covered by this policy unless explicitly stated.

4.1 Primary caregivers are entitled to 90 calendar days of paid parental leave, inclusive of weekends and public holidays falling within the period.
4.2 Secondary caregivers are entitled to 14 calendar days of paid parental leave, which may be split into two blocks within 6 months of the birth or adoption date, subject to manager agreement on timing.
4.3 Parental leave must be requested at least 30 days before the expected start date, except in cases of premature birth or medical emergency, where retroactive approval within 7 days of the leave starting is permitted.
4.4 Adoptive parents are entitled to the same parental leave terms as biological parents, effective from the date of legal custody transfer.

6.1 Employees may take up to 3 days of emergency leave per year for family emergencies, bereavement, or unforeseen circumstances, without advance notice, subject to notifying the manager within 24 hours by any reasonable means (call, message, or email).
6.2 Emergency leave beyond 3 days in a year is deducted from the annual leave balance, or treated as unpaid leave if the annual balance is exhausted.

5.1 Unpaid leave of up to 30 days may be requested for personal reasons, subject to manager and HR approval. Approval is not guaranteed and depends on business need and prior leave usage patterns.
5.2 Unpaid leave exceeding 30 days requires Director-level approval and may affect benefit continuity, including health insurance coverage, which is suspended after 45 consecutive days of unpaid leave unless the employee opts to self-fund premiums during that period.
